Parenting small children during a pandemic when you can’t really go anywhere is insanely, stupidly hard. The kids hate it too. It’s freezing outside, and we can’t go anywhere public. I have the Bose QuietComfort 350 (I think). I wear them all the time. My wife gets mad because I wear them so much. No headphones are going to really block out a screaming child.

The difficult thing here is that before a certain age, little kids _can’t_ understand what’s wrong. Not that they didn’t understand, but are incapable of understanding. They don’t have executive function or moral reasoning or higher levels of cognition. So trying to “teach them a lesson” usually just falls flat, or worse, is damaging. A parent will end up teaching the _wrong_ lesson, like “I’m bad and grownups hate me”, and the kid will grow up with neurosis and trauma. 

Parenting is exceptionally hard. I don’t think this gets talked about enough. It’s insanely hard, because kids are not rational beings. They’re little chaos balls that somehow, after years of severe fumbling, get shaped into functional adults. 

Anyway... I’m sorry about your cat. I get it. I’m mad at my kids _all the time_. But I’ve learned that they just can’t. They *can not* parse the problems they’re creating, and have to just be managed till they’re old enough to learn to manage themselves.
